notes: Hiphil is used intransitively/statively here, not causatively: both citations (Dan.10.11 "I stood trembling"; Ezra.10.9 "the people sat trembling") describe the SUBJECT itself trembling, not the subject causing something else to tremble. Kept as "tremble" per the person's given gloss, which matches the actual usage; flagging the unusual (non-causative) hiphil pattern.
Gloss collision: "tremble" (exact) matches FIVE existing root-level glosses -- זוע (H2111), ערץ (H6206), ירע (H3415), רגז (H7264), and חרד (H2729) -- disambiguating search alias added.
